quickAnswer: Massachusetts public school calendars are set by local districts, so first day, last day, February recess, April recess, holidays, staff days, and make-up day plans vary by district. Boston Public Schools uses staggered opening dates and publishes official English and translated calendar files, so families should verify the date that applies to their school and grade group.
about:
Massachusetts public school calendars are approved locally by each district, with state rules requiring at least 180 school days for public school students. Families should not assume that Boston, nearby suburban districts, and regional school systems share the same first day, recess weeks, professional development days, or last-day timing.

The Massachusetts calendar pattern is distinctive because many districts schedule both February recess and April spring recess. That differs from states that use one spring break period, and it matters for child care, shared custody schedules, youth programs, family travel, and summer camp planning.

Boston Public Schools is the current reviewed Massachusetts district on MySchoolDates. BPS publishes districtwide calendars, official PDFs, and translated calendar files for multilingual families. The Boston calendar also uses staggered opening dates, so families should confirm whether the listed date applies to their school, grade group, or program.

calendarRules.description: Massachusetts public schools generally schedule at least 180 school days, but districts may include make-up language or revise calendars after cancellations.

calendarRules.label: February and April recess
calendarRules.description: Many Massachusetts districts use a February recess around Presidents Day and an April spring recess around Patriots' Day week.

calendarRules.label: Staggered openings
calendarRules.description: Large districts such as Boston may publish different first days for grade groups, schools, or programs rather than one opening date for every student.

calendarRules.label: Translated calendars
calendarRules.description: Some districts publish translated calendar PDFs. Families should treat translated files as versions of the same district calendar unless the district identifies a separate program calendar.

faqs.a: Massachusetts school start dates vary by district. Many districts begin in late August or early September, but families should select their district calendar to confirm the official first day.

faqs.q: Are Massachusetts school calendars the same statewide?
faqs.a: No. Massachusetts public school calendars are set locally by district, so first day, last day, recess weeks, staff days, and make-up rules can differ.

faqs.q: How many school days are required in Massachusetts?
faqs.a: Massachusetts public schools generally schedule at least 180 school days. District calendars may also include built-in make-up days or revision language for cancellations.

faqs.q: Do Massachusetts schools have February vacation?
faqs.a: Many Massachusetts districts schedule a February recess around Presidents Day, followed by another spring recess in April. Exact dates vary by district.

faqs.q: Where can I find the Boston Public Schools calendar?
faqs.a: Use the Boston Public Schools calendar page on MySchoolDates for BPS staggered start dates, holidays, winter recess, February recess, April spring recess, official PDF links, translated calendar files, and calendar downloads.

faqs.q: Does Boston Public Schools publish translated calendars?
faqs.a: Yes. BPS publishes translated versions of the district calendar for multiple languages. Families should still verify changes on the official BPS district calendar page.

faqs.q: Can I add a Massachusetts school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. District pages on MySchoolDates include calendar download options when available, including ICS files that can be imported into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook.
